artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1758: A "Deliziosa" with Hanging Gardens
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Pozzi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an elaborate architectural structure with a central monument and surrounding colonnades. The composition features a grand central staircase leading up to a large platform adorned with a sculptural group including horses and a large obelisk-like structure at the center. Flanking the stairs and the central monument are symmetrical sections with ornamental pillars topped with finials. The scene is further adorned with sculptural reliefs and figures in various poses. Below, the foreground depicts a scene of various animals and small human-like figures. The drawing showcases intricate architectural details and decorative elements typical of grand ceremonial structures.

artworks.description: The image shows an ornate architectural structure with a tall, intricately adorned tower in the center, flanked by lavishly decorated canopies supported by columns. The sky is filled with artistic, flowing clouds. The artwork features detailed brushwork or etching, employing fine lines for depth and texture. The color palette is monochromatic, with dark lines against a lighter background. Several figures are depicted close to us, engaging in various activities, while the architecture dominates the view in the distance.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1759: A Fortress

artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows an architectural drawing viewed from a slightly elevated point. The structure is symmetrical with a central round tower decorated with statues and cloud-like elements. Flanking the central tower are square towers with flags. The background features a sky filled with detailed clouds. The drawing is in a monochromatic color palette with precise line engraving depicting textures, forms, and shadows. Figures in period attire and a carriage are in the foreground, adding a human scale. Further back, bridges and windows adorn the walls.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1759: A "Deliziosa" with a Bacchanal

artworks.description: The structured landscape is depicted from an elevated point of view, showing architectural elements and a gathering. The horizon is close to the top, with trees, a canopy, symmetrical buildings with windows, flags, and a wall with an arched entrance. A horse-drawn carriage passes through the entrance. The scene is detailed with fine linework and shading, creating texture in the clouds and trees. The color palette is monochromatic, using shades of gray and sepia. People are gathered under the canopy, adding liveliness to the scene.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1760: The Temple of Neptune
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows an architectural drawing viewed from a direct frontal perspective. In the midsection is an ornate, circular temple-like structure with classical columns and detailed reliefs. Flanking the central edifice are two towering columns, each adorned with relief carvings and topped with a platform. Ships are depicted on either side of the temple. Close to us, several figures and a cart are engaged in various activities. The background features swirling clouds filling the sky. The color palette is monochromatic with varying tones of sepia. The artwork is characterized by meticulous linear detailing and cross-hatching techniques.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1760: A Chinoiserie Pavilion
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows an elevated theatrical or ceremonial scene viewed from a slightly lower angle. The scene features intricate architectural elements and a grand stage or pavilion adorned with a richly decorated canopy, sculptural figures, and a large vase or urn at the top. Surrounding the structure are arches resembling palm trees, under which figures are depicted. The style is detailed with fine lines, giving it an etching or engraving appearance. The color palette consists of shades of sepia or brown, creating a classic look. In the foreground, there is a group of people and animals engaged in a procession or gathering, with a staircase leading to the pavilion, emphasizing its grandeur and ceremonial nature.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1761: The Salubrious Baths
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image depicts an architectural stage or theatre set design with detailed classical elements. The central staircase leads to a columned structure adorned with statues and fabric. Flanking sections contain more statues and chandeliers, with trees and garlands around the stage. Figures and carriages are in the foreground, adding to the lively atmosphere.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1761: A Magnificent Theater
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This drawing depicts an elaborate architectural stage set. It illustrates a grand Baroque theater scene with intricate columns, statues, and decorative reliefs. The scene features an ornate façade framing a classical landscape in the background. Two turret-like structures with balconies and sculptures are shown emitting streams of smoke. Below, there are horse-drawn carriages and figures in various poses, creating a bustling and grandiose scene. The style reflects the opulence and theatricality typical of Baroque design.

artworks.description: The image is an architectural rendering seen from the front, displaying a symmetrical and detailed perspective of a grand building. The horizon line is low, the structure showcases elaborate engravings, statues on columns and obelisks. People can be seen nearby, and the color palette consists of subdued earthy tones with stylized clouds in the sky.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1762: A Kiosk, or Pleasure-House in Ottoman Style

artworks.description: This image shows a grand architectural structure designed in a classical style, featuring a symmetrical facade with multiple tiers adorned with columns and decorative elements. The sky above has a few soft clouds, and the color palette includes muted earthy tones such as beige, brown, and gray. The illustration captures intricacies like flora and ornamentation on the building's facade. Figures, including people and animals, are depicted in a courtly or ceremonial scene. Trees and sculptural elements are also present on both sides of the structure.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1763: The Grape Harvest

artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image features a grand architectural setting viewed from a frontal perspective. The horizon is obscured by large buildings and architectural elements. On each side, there are symmetrical buildings with decorative details, with fireworks bursting above them. In the center is a garden feature or fountain with lush vegetation and statues. The image is detailed with fine lines and textures, creating a sense of grandeur. The color palette is primarily brown, giving an antique look. There are figures engaged in activities throughout the landscape, adding a dynamic quality. In the distance, dense foliage and trees frame the scene.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1764: A Capitol Building

artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an architectural structure. The image depicts a grand, symmetrical building with classical architectural elements such as Corinthian columns, arched arcades, and statues. The building is elevated on a platform with two sweeping staircases. Statues of lions and human figures adorn the parapets. The foreground features a procession scene with horse-drawn carriages and figures. The sky is filled with decorative clouds. The drawing is richly detailed, showcasing intricate engraving craftsmanship.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1764: A  Magnificent Gallery Illuminated at Night

artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an ornate architectural facade. The image depicts a grandiose structure with elaborate decorations, columns, and statues, appearing to be the front of a building. The structure is richly adorned with detailed sculptures and drapery. Below the structure, a busy scene unfolds with numerous figures involved in various activities. The attention to detail in both the architecture and the figures adds depth and complexity to the scene.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1765: The Garden of the Hesperides
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image displays a detailed architectural scene with a focus on an elaborate building facade. The structure is adorned with sculptures, columns, and relief work. The scene features fine lines and engravings, showcasing a classical architectural style. The color palette is primarily sepia. Small boats are docked nearby, with figures engaging in activities. In the distance, sailing ships and fountains can be seen. Softly rendered clouds fill the sky above.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1765: A Decorated Building with Cockaigne Poles

artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image depicts an architectural façade with classical elements. The building is adorned with statues, flags, and decorative garlands. It has multiple levels with open windows showing interior figures, and the façade is detailed with reliefs and classical columns. In the foreground, there is a large procession with figures and horse-drawn carriages moving past the structure. The sky has soft clouds.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1766: The Palace of Orpheus
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image displays a grand architectural scene with an elaborate, arched structure viewed straight-on. The structure is symmetrical and adorned with statues, decorative elements, and figures. The horizon line is not visible, and the color palette is muted with sepia tones. Figures and animals populate the scene in a pastoral setting, and the etched lines provide detailed architectural and figure elements, giving depth and texture to the image.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1766: A Theater for Athletic Games
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a grand architectural stage set design. The image depicts an ornate, theatrical stage architecture designed in a classical style. The structure features a central grand entrance adorned with drapery and flanked by symmetrical, tiered galleries filled with figures engaged in various activities. These galleries have multiple levels with columned divisions and are populated with spectators or performers. At the top of the central part of the building is a clock framed by figurative decorations. The foreground shows an outdoor scene with people and animals. The drawing captures the grandeur and detailed craftsmanship of a baroque-style architectural fantasy, reminiscent of an 18th-century theatrical set, with meticulous attention to ornamental detail and compositional balance.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1767: A Triumphal Arch with the Farnese Hercules
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image features an architectural scene with a grand structure viewed from a slightly elevated perspective. The focus is on the elaborate triumphal arch adorned with decorative sculptures and reliefs. The intricate details of the structure are highlighted by fine linework, creating a textured appearance. Flanking the arch are dynamic fountains. The color palette is monochromatic in various shades of sepia. Figures and horses near the arch suggest movement and beyond them are dramatic stairs leading up to the structure.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1767: Mount Etna with the Forge of Vulcan
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image displays an engraving of a grand, theatrical scene viewed from a slightly elevated perspective. It features a rocky structure with statues dominating the center. Atop the rocks, a charioteer with flowing drapery is posed dramatically. Sculptures of mounted figures on plinths frame the scene on either side. The engraving showcases intricate lines for textures and a monochromatic color palette of gray and white for contrast. Figures and chariots in the forefront are animated, while additional statuary and embellishments populate the distant rocky backdrop.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1769: A "Deliziosa"
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows an architectural perspective in a classical style with detailed engravings. The scene features a grand building with symmetrical features, adorned with statues such as rearing horses and a central figure atop the roof. In the foreground, there are people, sculptures, obelisks, and a staircase leading up to the building. The technique used is fine lines and shading for depth and texture, typical of an engraving or etching. The color palette is monochromatic with sepia tones. In the background, there are hints of foliage, statues, and a cloudy sky.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1769: A Building for Public Entertainment
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an elaborate architectural facade. The artwork showcases a large classical structure adorned with intricate details and decorations. At the center, there is a grand stage-like area with tall columns supporting a richly decorated entablature. Above, there is a series of statues and figures situated next to an ornate clock. The facade features multiple levels with draperies hanging gracefully. In the foreground, there are two horse-drawn carriages on either side. The entire scene is set against a backdrop of a cloudy sky. The artwork is finely detailed, capturing the grandeur of public entertainment structures.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1770: An Roman Building for Commerce
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows an architectural structure with statues and a decorated facade. People and carriages are in front of the building, while festivities seem to be happening in the background. Trees and sculptural details flank the building, and the sky above shows clouds and stylized fireworks or smoke.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1770: The Fish Market Portico
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows a grand architectural structure with a decorative façade. The viewpoint is eye-level, offering a direct perspective. The structure is adorned with drapery and canopies, reaching towards the sky. Figures are visible near and far along the base, suggesting a gathering. The sky has swirling clouds depicted in cross-hatching. The color palette is primarily sepia, giving a historical feel. Luxurious materials are intricately detailed, evoking opulence and celebration.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1771: The Temple of Asclepius
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Vasi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image is an intricate black and white engraving of an architectural scene. A grand, domed temple with ornate details and sculptured figures is seen from a straight-on viewpoint. Swirling clouds in the sky provide a backdrop. The engraving features precise lines, creating realism and depth. Figures are in the middle ground, engaging in various activities. Lush trees and foliage are visible further back. The grayscale palette accentuates textures and shadows. The image conveys grandeur and historical elegance through architecture and detail.
